Container.Name: Unraid-Home
Container.Overview:
Self-populating homepage for your Unraid server. Scans Docker for containers and shows each one as a tile with its WebUI link, icon and status. Edit mode (from your home network) lets you rename, regroup, pin and hide tiles, add links and pages, and pick themes. Optional: login with authenticator sign-in, alerts (ntfy, Gotify, Discord, webhook, email), uptime and update badges, server stats, and automation for Nginx Proxy Manager and Cloudflare Tunnel so your apps get internet addresses automatically. All settings are optional.
Almost everything is set on the homepage itself: click Settings (home network only). What you set there is saved in /config/options.json. Only the few values on this template page that the container needs before it can start (the Docker address, proxy trust, the password and the mapped folders) stay here.
Email alerts with Gmail need an app password (https://myaccount.google.com/apppasswords), not your normal Google password.
Built entirely by AI (Claude, by Anthropic). Features are tested, but not every situation has been, so do your own due diligence before exposing it to the internet: keep the login on, use a strong password and 2FA, and review your Cloudflare, proxy and firewall settings. Use at your own risk.
Container.Changes:
### 2026-10-23 - 1.11.0: visitors on Tailscale or WireGuard are recognised: their tiles use the address they opened the page by, and apps with Tailscale turned on can open at their own Tailscale address (Links: Server / Tailscale).
### 2026-10-22 - 1.10.2: proxy hosts that forward to the container name count as working, so their internet addresses appear in the bookmarks file and the remote view. - 1.10.1: the bookmarks file now comes from a Bookmarks link beside the clock, in a small window, instead of Edit mode. - 1.10.0: download every app as a browser bookmarks file, in one "Server" folder (Edit mode > Browser bookmarks).
### 2026-10-20 - 1.9.2: tiles on the remote view show the address they open, so the Internet / Home network switch visibly changes them. - 1.9.1: the icon now loads from the main branch of Unraid-CA-Apps, like the template itself. - 1.9.0: the remote view only shows apps that really have a proxy host, and when signed in it can switch to your home-network links. - 1.8.0: Add all missing and Remove all on the Proxies page, and a per-app Auto-create choice so automatic creation never makes hosts you do not want. - 1.7.2: a proxy host that points somewhere else can be removed from the Proxies page too, after a second confirmation. - 1.7.1: proxy hosts have their own Proxies page, opened from a button at the top, with filters and automatic-creation controls. - 1.7.0: full control of Nginx Proxy Manager proxy hosts from the dashboard: remove a host, mark an app "no proxy", see hidden apps that are still reachable, and choose whether automatic creation covers only new containers or every app.
### 2026-10-19 - 1.6.0: a small clock beside the page title: digital, analog or both, with face, 24-hour, seconds and date options on the Settings page. - 1.5.0: settings now live on the Settings page. The template keeps only what the container needs to start (Docker address, proxy trust, password, mapped folders). Anything you already set here is still used, and the page's own values win over it. - 1.4.0: a Settings page on the homepage can now change every option, grouped and explained. What you set there is saved in /config/options.json; the variables you set are copied there on first start. - 1.3.0: your home network no longer needs a login by default (REQUIRE_LOGIN_LAN=true restores it); separate sign-in timeouts for home and internet, also settable on the page. - 1.2.0: history also records scans for non-existent paths, which apps get opened, the sign-in method used, and per-app availability. - 1.1.0: visitor history and dashboard (page loads, sign-ins, blocked requests) kept as plain files in /config/analytics, reachable from a Visitors button on the LAN. Connection status for Nginx Proxy Manager and Cloudflare.
### 2026-10-18 - 1.0.1: security review fixes (proxy-header handling, lockout limits). Socket-proxy setup documented. - 1.0.0: first stable release.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port the homepage is served on

Config.Name: Docker socket
Config.Description: Used to discover containers (and, only if you turn on Container controls, to start/stop/restart them). Note: the read-only flag does not limit what the Docker API allows.

Config.Name: Unraid templates
Config.Description: Optional. Lets the hover summaries use each app's Overview text from its Unraid template. Read-only; only the name, repository, overview, category and Tailscale settings are read. Also tells the page which apps have Tailscale turned on, so visitors on Tailscale can open them at their Tailscale address.

Config.Name: Config
Config.Description: Stores your settings, tile overrides, custom links and visitor history

Config.Name: Update status file
Config.Description: Optional. Lets tiles show an Update badge for containers Unraid says are out of date. Read-only.

Config.Name: Disk stats: array
Config.Description: Optional. Read-only. Lets the stats strip show array usage.

Config.Name: Disk stats: cache
Config.Description: Optional. Read-only. Lets the stats strip show cache usage.

Config.Name: Password
Config.Description: Login password (12+ characters). Leave blank to have one generated on first start; it is printed once in this container's log and stored only as a salted hash. This is the one setting the Settings page cannot change; use Change password there instead once the container is running.

Config.Name: Docker address
Config.Description: Where to ask about containers. Leave as-is when the Docker socket above is mapped in. Use tcp://docker-socket-proxy:2375 if you run a socket proxy instead (recommended when this page is reachable from the internet). Settings page shows this one read-only.

Config.Name: Trust proxy headers
Config.Description: On (default) believes the address headers from a reverse proxy or Cloudflare tunnel on your network, so the real visitor address and country are recorded. Turn off only if nothing in front of this page adds those headers. Settings page shows this one read-only.
